papers.title: Inhibition-related connectivity predicts irritability risk and resilience across early adolescence.
papers.abstract: Elevated irritability may in part arise from altered top-down networks, such as those implicated in inhibitory control, that may help modulate temper outbursts. Studies have linked higher youth irritability with aberrant neural patterns during inhibitory control; however, how these networks may relate to trajectories of irritability across key transitions, such as that from childhood to adolescence, remains unknown. Using data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study (N = 5,373), four previously identified irritability symptoms trajectories from baseline to 4-year follow-up (low-stable, high-decreasing, low-increasing, and high-chronic) were used to predict neural patterns during the baseline Stop Signal Task. Analyses examined associations between trajectories and whole brain activation and functional connectivity. Amygdala connectivity with insula during successful inhibition was lower in the high-decreasing compared to low-stable and low-increasing trajectories. During failed inhibition, amygdala and strital-prefrontal connectivity was lower in the low-increasing compared to the low-stable and high-chronic irritability trajectories. Results remained after controlling for baseline irritability. Findings indicate that changes in inhibitory control networks in preadolescents may contribute to high-decreasing and low-increasing irritability trajectories across early adolescence. Unexpectedly, differences between the high-chronic and low-stable trajectories were nonsignificant, suggesting inhibitory control may affect changes in irritability symptoms rather than their levels.
papers.summary: 本研究利用青少年大腦認知發展研究（ABCD Study）的5,373名受試者數據，探討青春期早期抑制控制相關的神經網路如何預測長達四年的易怒症狀軌跡。研究發現，在成功抑制反應時，杏仁核與腦島的連結性降低與「高下降型」易怒軌跡相關；而在抑制失敗時，杏仁核與紋狀體-前額葉的連結性降低則與「低上升型」軌跡有關。這些神經連結差異在控制基線易怒水準後依然顯著。
papers.significance: 此研究揭示了前青少年期抑制控制網路的改變會影響青春期早期易怒症狀的變化軌跡（如改善或惡化），而非決定其絕對的嚴重程度。這項發現為理解兒童過渡到青春期時的情緒調節機制提供了重要的神經生物學視角，有助於未來針對不同易怒發展風險的青少年制定精準的預防與介入策略。
